MARKET.head: Australian wine exports fall 7% as US slump offsets Canada and Thailand gains
MARKET.summ:
Australian wine exports declined overall in the year ending September 2026, but the results varied significantly across markets. Strong growth in Southeast Asia and Canada was offset by more challenging conditions in the United States (US). 

This Market Bulletin will analyse the latest export data, released...
takeaways: Australian wine exports fell 7% in value to $2.25 billion in the 12 months to September 2026, with volume down 5%.
US exports dropped 28% in value to $219 million, the largest driver of the volume decline, amid tariffs and weak demand.
Canada grew 12% in value to $185 million as American wines were pulled from shelves in the Canada-US trade dispute.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux leads fine wine trade at 39.6% of value, Lafite top wine
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux led the market, claiming 39.6%, Lafite accounting for over a quarter of its trade
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 39.6% of traded fine wine value this week, with Lafite accounting for over a quarter of the region's value.
Burgundy slipped to 18.4% from 24.8% last week, while Tuscany rose from 5.2% to 8.9%.
Bollinger overtook Dom Perignon and Louis Roeder as the top-traded Champagne producer by value.

MARKET.head: Booze News Weekly Roundup covers Uncle Nearest sale, wine heist, and product drops
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. This week, we have updates on Uncle Nearest’s potential buyers, Mark Zuckerberg’s Guinness flop, the latest product releases, and more.
takeaways: Uncle Nearest is reportedly nearing a sale, with potential buyers now in talks, per VinePair's weekly roundup.
Southern Glazer's faces a bribery snafu, and OpenTable published its 2026 restaurant report this week.
VinePair's weekly roundup also lists new product releases ahead of the holiday gifting season.

MARKET.head: Vinitaly.USA debuts in New York City at Pier 36 this October
MARKET.summ: The Italian wine trade event makes its New York City debut October 26 and 27, bringing 300 exhibitors and 2,500 wines to Pier 36
takeaways: Vinitaly.USA, organized by Veronafiere with the Italian Trade Agency, holds its first New York City edition October 26 and 27, 2026 at Pier 36.
The event moves from Chicago, where it ran for two years, and will host 300 exhibitors presenting 2,500 labels.
Italian regions Asti DOCG, Sicilia DOC, Prosecco DOC, plus Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Lazio and Sardinia collectives, will exhibit; registration is open.

CULTURE.head: Real Housewives shows reveal the mass-market wines their cast actually drinks
CULTURE.summ: What do the reality stars’ drinking habits reveal about wealth, taste, status and the economics of the U.S. wine industry?
takeaways: Essayist Cake Zine contributor notes Real Housewives cast favour mass-market, high-alcohol, sweet California cabernet over fine wine.
Whitney Rose's recommendation of Justin Cabernet, sold at Walgreens for $22, shows the cast's price-insensitive yet mainstream taste.
Mary Cosby praised the 2003 Dom Pérignon vintage as the 'best' because its heatwave-ripened grapes were sweeter.

CULTURE.head: Cloudy and unfiltered wines gain shelf space as pét nat spreads in supermarkets
CULTURE.summ:
There’s something refreshing about unfiltered or unfined wines. We filter through a selection …

Centuries ago, Geoffrey Chaucer observed that “ther is no newe gyse that it nas old”. This truth - that there is nothing new under the sun - certainly applies to wine: every year, a well-documented or ancient viticultural...
takeaways: Marks & Spencer's Trouble organic rosé is the first cloudy still wine sold in a British supermarket, at £12.
Pét nat is an ancestral method bottled before fermentation finishes, so it stays cloudy with dead yeast cells.
Ottolenghi's Zainab Majerikova says unfiltered house wines add texture and suit foods with big, complex flavours.

CULTURE.head: Europe bartenders say American drinkers are curious, though they still favor vodka
CULTURE.summ: Over decades of regular trips to Europe, Regine Rousseau, the Chicago-based founder of wine marketing and events consultancy Shall We Wine, never really subscribed to the directive often preached by U.S. travel publications: When traveling abroad, try not to let your American show. “Number one: I like wearing really bright...
takeaways: European bartenders say American bar guests are engaged and curious, with conversation starting as soon as they sit down.
Americans often order Martinis made with vodka and request US spirit substitutions, while adventurous travellers embrace local drinks like Porto tonics.
US visitors to Europe reached a record 24 million trips in 2025, per The Wall Street Journal.

SCIENCE.head: UK vineyards navigate early, warm, dry 2026 harvest after frost
SCIENCE.summ: After a run of dramatically different vintages, 2026 has given UK viticulture another season that challenged assumptions, but also demonstrated just how much English and Welsh vineyards can achieve. The 2026 growing season began with a series of extraordinary frost events, creating a challenging start before developing into a...
takeaways: A 2026 season began with extraordinary frost events, then turned warm and dry with exceptionally rapid ripening across English and Welsh vineyards.
Harvest arrived several weeks early at some sites, with dry weather cutting disease pressure and yielding clean fruit.
Growers now treat soil health, water management, canopy protection and maturity monitoring as ongoing resilience measures rather than crisis responses.

SCIENCE.head: Domaine Bousquet details organic and water-saving practices at Mendoza winery visit
SCIENCE.summ: Domaine Bousquet continues to elevate Argentine wine through generations of dedication and innovation in organic wine practices. Earlier this year, Irma Remigio and her team warmly welcomed SWR’s Membership Manager, Ilva Fridenberga, to their winery. The winery, located at the foot of the Andes Mountains, is globally recognized...
takeaways: SWR membership manager Ilva Fridenberga visited Domaine Bousquet in Mendoza, Argentina, in February, hosted by Irma Remigio.
The winery is trialling biodiversity and garden vineyard corridors, with harvest done from outside the vine rows.
It switched to high-pressure hoses to cut water use and updated tanks and temperature-controlled rooms to save energy.

SCIENCE.head: MODIS satellite data validated for estimating vineyard water use in Italy
SCIENCE.summ: In North-Eastern Italy water demand for vineyards irrigation is constantly increasing, but this conflicts with the high civil and industrial rates of water consumptions in the area, which is one of the most densely populated in Europe
takeaways: Researchers at the University of Padova developed a remote-sensing method using MODIS satellite data to map vineyard evapotranspiration in North-Eastern Italy.
Estimates were calibrated on two years of data and independently validated against four years of eddy-covariance measurements from a 25-hectare vineyard.
Results showed good consistency with in situ observations, suggesting MODIS could monitor vineyard water consumption at the regional scale.

SCIENCE.head: Newick Wine Estate in East Sussex planted 37,000 vines in 2023
SCIENCE.summ: Newick Wine Estate in East Sussex is a place of outstanding tranquillity. Newick Village is situated almost equal distance from both Canterbury and Winchester, two important Cathedral cities in the south of England. It is not surprising therefore that the village has an ancient history.
takeaways: Jonathan and Charlotte Sharpe planted 37,000 vines across half of their 16-hectare East Sussex farm at Newick Wine Estate in 2023.
Ten frost events in 2026, four of them severe, damaged the vines, and the last frost came on 10 May.
The team is trialling methods to control spotted wing drosophila (SWD), with the GM20 Pinot Noir clone unaffected in 2025.

SCIENCE.head: Grenache rootstocks and irrigation shape vine water use in NE Spain
SCIENCE.summ: Under the context of global change, any decrease in water use by crops is essential, because water is becoming a more and more scarce resource, especially in Mediterranean areas, where grapevines are grown
takeaways: A three-year NE Spain trial grafted Grenache onto 110-R, 41-B and 161-49C rootstocks, with irrigated and non-irrigated plots.
Water use efficiency was higher in non-irrigated vines, and higher on 110-R and 41-B than on 161-49C.
Stomatal control in irrigated vines appeared driven more by hormonal than hydraulic signals, the researchers suggest.

SCIENCE.head: Italian researchers push genetic diversity and climate-ready vines for future viticulture
SCIENCE.summ: In the globalization conditions possible future scenarios, optimistic and pessimistic are supposed
takeaways: Pisa University authors argue climate change may extend viticulture into higher latitudes and altitudes, needing more resilient genotypes.
They warn local grapevine varieties are being abandoned, so Italian regions started projects to recover them and preserve biodiversity.
The paper reports viticultural and economic trials on Malvasia of Lazio, Cesanese d'Affile and Cabernet Sauvignon under Cordon Spur of Conegliano training.

SCIENCE.head: Conegliano pruning trials on Lazio grape varieties test yield, quality and profit
SCIENCE.summ: In this work the salient results of the viticultural and ecomomic researches earned out on interesting italic varieties of Latium (Malvasia of the Lazio and Cesanese d'Affile) and an international vsriety (Cabernet sauvignon), "Cordon Spur of Conegliano" (CSC) as growing system, will be exposed
takeaways: CRA, ARSIAL, University of Tuscia and University of Padova researchers studied Conegliano growing systems on Malvasia di Lazio, Cesanese d'Affile and Cabernet Sauvignon.
They compared Vertical Tridimensional Minimal Pruning of Conegliano with and without the DMRC double-maturation technique, aiming to raise gross saleable product.
The authors state that climate-driven fertility can cause overcropping and lower wine quality, and that water scarcity makes reduced vine water use essential.

SCIENCE.head: Vine balance explained: how growth and crop load shift across the season
SCIENCE.summ: Vine balance is a commonly used term in viticulture that expresses the concept of an appropriate balance of vegetative to reproductive growth of the vine
takeaways: Vine balance is a viticulture concept describing the balance of vegetative and reproductive vine growth.
A balanced vine ripens its crop, sets fruitful buds for next year, and builds reserves.
Standard indirect measures like yield to pruning weight ratio do not capture seasonal growth dynamics.

SCIENCE.head: Winter vineyard jobs eased by pruners, subsoilers and frost-protection tools
SCIENCE.summ: As autumn turns to winter a list of jobs looms large in the calendar. The vines need pruning and the soil needs care and attention. To make these jobs less demanding and costly, different tools can be used.
takeaways: Vineyard Magazine describes winter vineyard tasks: pruning, soil care, and frost protection against late spring losses.
Cordless battery secateurs and a tractor-mounted pre-pruner are presented as ways to speed up pruning.
A two-leg subsoiler with J-shaped legs loosens soil compacted by tractor tyres in a wide band.

SCIENCE.head: English and Welsh vintage 2026 picked early, with frost cutting volumes
SCIENCE.summ: Record-early starts, ripe and healthy fruit, and a season that kept teams on their toes. Spring frost left its mark on some, but the mood across the industry is one of real excitement. As I look back to last year’s report of earliest on record, 2026 seemed in a hurry to beat it.
takeaways: Gusbourne in Kent began picking Pinot Noir on 26 August, two weeks ahead of 2025.
Nyetimber in West Sussex started picking on 14 September, five days ahead of its 2018 record.
Spring frosts killed early shoots at The Grange in Hampshire, reducing yields even as fruit quality stayed high.

SCIENCE.head: Vineyard irrigation water chemistry shapes soil nutrients, structure and salinity risk
SCIENCE.summ: THURSDAY, OCTOBER 8, 2026. BY STAN GRANT, VITICULTURIST. Part Two of a Three-Part Vineyard Mineral Nutrient Management Lab Analysis Series.
takeaways: Nearly pure snowmelt water strips soil minerals, making soils more acidic, less permeable and prone to crusting.
Alkaline well water can supply calcium and magnesium but carbonates precipitate them, reducing their fertilizer value.

SCIENCE.head: Ethephon and manual thinning cut Portuguese Vinhos Verdes yields by up to 70%
SCIENCE.summ: Some years, climate conditions and biological events increment the fertility of vines, which can lead to over cropping and a decrease of wine quality
takeaways: A 2007 Vinhos Verdes trial tested yield control on Loureiro and Borraçal vines using chemicals and manual bunch thinning.
Ethephon and manual thinning significantly reduced crop; Borraçal yield fell about 41% under manual thinning, Loureiro about 26%.
Ethephon at buck-shot stage raised sugar and lowered acidity in Loureiro, but manual thinning brought no quality gains in either variety.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The 2025 wines from Pascal Jolivet in Sancerre
NEWSLETTERS.summ: These are the 2025 releases from leading Sancerre-based producer Pascal Jolivet. This was a good vintage, but not
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Pascal Jolivet's 2025 Sancerre-area releases were reviewed, with the vintage described as good but not simple, following a dry, warm spring and an August heatwave.
Sancerre's 2025 harvest was late August and early September, with rapid sugar accumulation, producing rich, ripe wines that searched for definition and typicity.
The Jolivet Sauvage Sancerre 2025, a parcel from 2 hectares in Champtin and Bué-en-Sancerre, received the top score of 95/100 and was compared to Cotat in style.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Visiting the Vineyard in the Sky
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The extraordinary story of Domaine de Beudon in Valais, Switzerland
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Marion and Jacky Granges-Faiss farm Domaine de Beudon at 890 metres in Valais, Switzerland, a site reachable only by cable car or a 90-minute hike.
Jacky bought the estate in 1971; the family became Valais's first Demeter-certified estate in 1992, and Jacky died in June 2016 after a vineyard accident.
Beudon's six hectares produce wines with no added yeast since 2003 and sulphites as the only additive, but ferment and age partly at Pierre-Antoine Crettenand's winery in Saillon.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Nasty Not Nice
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Why are people drinking less, when wine is better than ever? I have an idea. Wine is too good.
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues wine is too pleasant and risk-free, and that the trade should add insecurity and difficulty to lure drinkers back.
He cites cork taint as a past thrill that has largely disappeared, and says wine sales were rising when TCA affected one in four or five bottles.
Atkin suggests bottling each barrel separately and selling Primeur allocations in a Smithfield-style cash scramble to restore excitement.

NEWSLETTERS.head: California Cult Bubbles and More: The Latest from Ultramarine & Cruse Wine Co.
NEWSLETTERS.summ: If there were a competition for California’s geekiest winemaker, I’m sure Michael Cruse would make the final round. His willingness
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow
takeaways: Michael Cruse, a California winemaker, is associated with Cruse Wine Co. and Ultramarine, per the Vinography piece.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Inside Chinon’s Lieux-Dits Project
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Vignerons lead a collective effort to recognize the vineyards behind the appellation’s Cabernet Francs
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Chinon's Syndicat began a long-term project in 2014 to promote lieux-dits, without a formal classification or technical criteria.
Seven lieux-dits have been officially recognized so far, starting with La Croix Boissée in Cravant-les-Côteaux in 2018.
Lieux-dits must be on the cadastre and named on at least two vignerons' labels, with each recognition backed by a monograph.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Yet Another Vintage Port Flex Post (Tasting Selections From 1985 - 2022)
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Last week, I published a bunch of reviews from an NYC media tasting of selections from the (stellar) 2024 Port vintage. I typically follow those type of posts up with another post of other, older selections of vintage Ports that I tasted at the same event, and I offer them without much shame as simply […] This article was...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude published reviews from an NYC media tasting of selections from the 2024 Port vintage, which it calls stellar.

NEWSLETTERS.head: N is for Noirien
NEWSLETTERS.summ: What eco-geotypes tell us about grape genetics, geography, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Noirien is an old French word for Pinot noir, from noir meaning black.
The Noirien group includes Pinot noir, Pinot gris, Pinot blanc, Pinot Meunier, Chardonnay, Gamay noir, Auxerrois and Melon.
Its zone runs from Champagne through the Côte d'Or to Beaujolais, and from the central Loire east to Alsace and the Jura.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Why Michelin Ratings Still Won’t Tell You Who Actually Made Your Burgundy Wine
NEWSLETTERS.summ: This wine guide explains why no critic's score, not even from a renowned guide like Michelin, truly reveals who made your regional wine. Consumer insight is key
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Since July, a growing number of Burgundy bottles carry Michelin ratings of one to three grapes, assessed against five criteria.
Michelin's criteria are agronomy, technical mastery, identity, balance and consistency, measuring quality against a fixed standard per vintage.
Burgundy labels print the appellation in large type and the domaine name in far smaller letters, a convention a Michelin rating does not change.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Telling a mountain to move
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Delving into the details of change in the DO Montsant wine region of Catalunya
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: DO Montsant, in Catalunya's Priorat area, has revised its bylaws to add certification for 'vi brisat' (orange-style) wines, as DO Terra Alta did in 2022.

Montsant's revised bylaws also create a 'minimal intervention' classification requiring mandatory hand-harvesting, organic certification, spontaneous fermentation, and a maximum sulfur dioxide limit far below conventional levels.
The DO has not disclosed the actual maximum SO2 limit, which the author requested and which is absent from the final bylaws posted online.

NEWSLETTERS.head: 400 Montepulciano Bottles for Thomas Jefferson circa 1805
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The wine everyone’s been gushing over since the middle ages!
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: A 1350 trade contract between the Del Pecora family and merchant Jacopo di Vanni is the oldest known document for Vino Nobile di Montepulciano.
Thomas Jefferson received 473 bottles of Montepulciano in November 1805 and requested 400 bottles annually afterward.
A 2024 document unveiled by the Consorzio del Vino Nobile di Montepulciano shows the term Vino Nobile was first used in 1766 by the Jesuits.
